outcomeNote: Narrative illustrating restraint from weekday thought on Shabbat

segments.he: אֵין מַחְשִׁיכִין. תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מַעֲשֶׂה בְּחָסִיד אֶחָד שֶׁנִּפְרְצָה לוֹ פִּרְצָה בְּתוֹךְ שָׂדֵהוּ וְנִמְלַךְ עָלֶיהָ לְגוֹדְרָהּ, וְנִזְכַּר שֶׁשַּׁבָּת הוּא, וְנִמְנַע אוֹתוֹ חָסִיד וְלֹא גְּדָרָהּ, וְנַעֲשָׂה לוֹ נֵס וְעָלְתָה בּוֹ צָלָף, וּמִמֶּנָּה הָיְתָה פַּרְנָסָתוֹ וּפַרְנָסַת אַנְשֵׁי בֵיתוֹ.
segments.en: We learned in the mishna that «one may not wait for nightfall» at the edge of the Shabbat boundary in order to hire workers or bring produce from outside of the boundary immediately after Shabbat. «The Sages taught: There was an incident with a pious man» in which «a breach was made in» the fence around «his field, and» when he saw it «he decided to fence it in. And» then «he remembered that it was Shabbat. And that pious man refrained from fixing the fence» forever because he had thought about fixing it on Shabbat. «And a miracle was done for him, and a caper bush grew in» the breach, thereby closing it up. «And from it» and its produce he then «received his livelihood and the livelihood of the members of his household.»
